::: {.eyebrow}
the model, from the ground up
:::

These pages explain what `plant` solves, why the model is built that way, and
how the pieces fit together. They bring material from papers and vignettes
into one route through the theory. The sections below, and the contents pane on
the left, follow the recommended reading order.

## 1. Foundations

Start here for the demographic framework shared by the biological models. If
you are new to `plant`, begin with the big picture. The next two pages introduce
the mathematics in stages before the full population equation.

- [The big picture](overview.qmd) — the mental model in plain language, no
  equations. **Start here.**
- [The maths, gently](maths-primer.qmd) — the core equations built up one step
  at a time.
- [The maths, worked through](from-primer-to-pde.qmd) — the same equations pushed
  through one small numerical example, bridging the primer and the full PDE.
- [The size-structured PDE](size-structured-pde.qmd) — demography of
  individuals, patches, and metacommunities.

## 2. Models and physiology {#models}

Next, see how different biological strategies supply growth, fecundity, and
mortality rates to the shared demographic framework. Begin with the
[models overview](models/index.qmd), then follow the models and physiological
processes in dependency order.

- [FF16](models/ff16.qmd) — the trait-based functional-balance model and the
  starting point for the more detailed physiology.
- [Assimilation & hydraulics](assimilation-hydraulics.qmd) — the leaf-level
  carbon and water economy.
- [TF24](models/tf24.qmd) — the hydraulically coupled leaf model, plus its TF24f
  acclimation-lag variant.
- [Soil water & root uptake](soil-water.qmd) — where transpired water comes
  from: the multi-layer soil balance and the root-collar solve that feeds it
  to the leaf model.
- [K93](models/k93.qmd) — Kohyama's basal-area competition model.

## 3. Adaptive dynamics

After learning how resident plants grow and compete, move on to invasion
fitness and evolutionary change.

- [Adaptive dynamics](adaptive-dynamics.qmd) — the main ideas and evolutionary
  endpoints.
- [Models in `regnans`](adaptive-dynamics/index.qmd) — four small models for
  learning and checking the workflow.
- [DD99](adaptive-dynamics/DD99.qmd) — competition and evolutionary branching.
- [GK98](adaptive-dynamics/GK98.qmd) — adaptation across different habitats.
- [GM99](adaptive-dynamics/GM99.qmd) — the evolution of seed size.
- [JJ12](adaptive-dynamics/JJ12.qmd) — the evolution of migratory arrival time.
- [Finding evolutionary attractors](adaptive-dynamics/solving_attractors.qmd) —
  selection gradients in the full `plant` model.
- [Community assembly with simple models](adaptive-dynamics/assembly.qmd) — how
  repeated invasion builds a community.
- [Maximum-fitness community assembly](adaptive-dynamics/assembly_fitmax.qmd) —
  assembly in `plant` using the best available mutant.
- [Stochastic assembly](adaptive-dynamics/assembly_stochastic.qmd) — assembly
  using random mutational steps.

## 4. Implementation {#implementation}

These pages explain how the equations are solved on a computer. See the
[implementation overview](implementation/index.qmd) for an introduction.

- [The characteristic method](implementation/characteristic-method.qmd)
- [ODE stepping & control](implementation/ode-stepping.qmd)
- [The node-spacing algorithm](implementation/node-spacing.qmd)
- [Canopy & light-environment models](implementation/canopy-models.qmd)

## 5. Prediction and reproducibility

Finish with two cross-cutting topics that matter when interpreting, comparing,
or forecasting with model results.

- [Uncertainty & prediction](uncertainty-partitioning.qmd) — where uncertainty
  enters a `plant` prediction, and how ensembles could be used to measure it.
- [Scientific versioning of models](models/scientific-versioning.qmd) — how to
  distinguish changes in the scientific model from changes in the software.
